text.p: The Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp (Pagcor) said on Friday it had rescinded the authority of Mondragon Leisure and Resorts Corp (MLRC) to operate a casino inside the Clark freeport area. "The board of directors of Pagcor has resolved to rescind MLRC's authority to operate the casino at the Clark Special Economic Zone. Accordingly, you are advised to cease and discontinue the operation of the Mimosa Regency Casino upon receipt of this letter," Alice Reyes, the chairwoman of state-run Pagcor, said in a letter.
Copies of the letter were distributed to the press.
Mondragon Leisure, a subsidiary of Mondragon International Philippines Inc, is the operator of a hotel inside the Clark zone.
Pagcor also operates a casino near the Clark zone.

Reyes said that Mondragon had continuously violated some provisions of their agreement stating that the Mondragon casino shall cater only to "foreigners, Filipino U.S. greencard holders and walk-in Filipino customers/casino players."

Reyes claimed Mondragon had come out with marketing strategies which actively enticed Filipinos to patronise the Mondragon casino by granting limousine services, reimbursement of incidental travel expenses, free use of its hotel rooms and discounts on losses of players.
"The above provisions contemplate that MLRC should tap the foreign market ... since the local market is being sufficiently serviced by the Pagcor casinos," she said.
"In fact, this matter has been stressed upon MLRC repeatedly in the course of the negotiations leading to the above-mentioned agreement," she added.
Mondragon officials were not immediately available for comment. A Clark resident said Mondragon had closed its casino on Thursday evening.
Mondragon shares have been declining in the past few days on persistent rumours of a pending closure, but Mondragon officials had dismissed the possibility.
However, Mondragon shares closed 65 centavos up at 10.25 pesos on Friday after the company announced positive forecasts for net profits in 1996 and 1997.
Earlier, a request by Mondragon for the suspension of its shares because of the dispute with Pagcor was denied by the Philippine stock exchange. The bourse did not give any reason.
